meta.scene_summary: We are currently in a race to build the future while accidentally deleting the privacy settings.

cooking.headline: The 20-year-old math mystery is solved, but the trust issues remain
cooking.summary: Security researchers finally cracked the seeds used for NIST elliptic curves, ending a two-decade-long cryptographic scavenger hunt. It turns out that even when the math is open source, we still spend twenty years treating it like a locked diary in a teen's bedroom.
cooking.plain_english: Security researchers have successfully determined the origin values used to create government-standardized elliptic curve cryptography, which were previously unknown.

cooking.headline: Firefox adds JPEG XL support, finally solving the 'my image is 4MB' problem
cooking.summary: Firefox is finally shipping JPEG XL by default, giving us a modern format that actually respects our bandwidth and storage. It's the digital equivalent of finally cleaning out your downloads folder after telling yourself you'd do it for three years.
cooking.plain_english: Firefox now supports the JPEG XL image format, which allows for higher quality images with smaller file sizes.

cooking.headline: Solar power just hit the 'actually useful' milestone by outpacing nuclear
cooking.summary: Solar energy has finally generated more electricity globally than nuclear, proving that the sun is finally pulling its weight in the production environment. It turns out that when you stop waiting for a fusion reactor to be finished and just point some panels at the sky, you eventually start seeing some real throughput.
cooking.plain_english: Global solar power generation has exceeded nuclear power generation for the first time.

cooking.headline: DeepSeek released a new model, which is roughly 45 seconds old
cooking.summary: DeepSeek just dropped another model update, proving that the shelf life of a 'state-of-the-art' AI is now shorter than a carton of milk. It is impressive, but at this point, you are basically trying to keep up with a treadmill that is set to Olympic sprinter speeds.
cooking.plain_english: DeepSeek has released a new version of its artificial intelligence model called v4.1 Flash.

cooked.headline: Meta's smart glasses are now recording by accident, not by design
cooked.summary: Meta confirmed that their smart glasses were recording footage without the indicator light turning on, effectively turning a wearable gadget into an accidental paparazzi device. It is the tech equivalent of your coworker forgetting to mute their mic during a meeting, except the mic is a camera and the meeting is your entire life.
cooked.plain_english: Meta has acknowledged a software bug that caused some of its smart glasses to record video without activating the required privacy indicator light.

cooked.headline: When your ad-tech target profiling includes 'political dissident'
cooked.summary: It turns out the ad-tech network you thought was just tracking your shoe size was actually a delivery pipeline for government-grade spyware. It's like finding out your local mail carrier is also a professional hitman.
cooked.plain_english: A digital advertising company was found to be distributing surveillance software capable of hacking mobile devices.

cooked.headline: Starlink's kill-switch is now a geopolitical side quest
cooked.summary: Musk reportedly asked Trump to throttle Starlink access in Ukraine, turning a satellite network into a literal bargaining chip for global policy. It is the ultimate 'I'm taking my ball and going home' move, but with orbital hardware instead of a football.
cooked.plain_english: Reports indicate that Elon Musk discussed limiting Starlink satellite internet services in Ukraine with Donald Trump during the conflict.

cooked.headline: The US federal deficit just hit $2 trillion, proving the government is allergic to profit margins
cooked.summary: The US federal budget deficit has ballooned to nearly $2 trillion, which is a fantastic way to handle personal finances if you don't care about ever being solvent. It's basically the macroeconomic equivalent of a startup burning through all their runway on office snacks and ping-pong tables.
cooked.plain_english: The United States federal government spent nearly $2 trillion more than it collected in revenue during the 2026 fiscal year.

cooked.headline: Meta's algorithm had a 'whoops' moment during the Brazil election
cooked.summary: Meta employees reportedly admitted that their systems throttled political accounts, proving once again that the algorithm is just a group project where nobody knows who actually pushed the faulty code. It's the digital equivalent of accidentally deleting the production database and blaming it on a mysterious 'configuration update.'
cooked.plain_english: Meta employees stated that the company's automated systems hindered the reach of accounts belonging to Brazilian President Lula during the election.

cooked.headline: Home Assistant is scanning your secrets, for your own good of course
cooked.summary: Home Assistant introduced an integration that scans your local secrets, which is exactly the kind of 'help' no developer ever asked for. It is like a landlord letting themselves into your apartment to reorganize your sock drawer while you are still sleeping.
cooked.plain_english: A new software update for Home Assistant includes a feature that automatically scans user configuration files for sensitive security keys.
